---
title: "Agents: instructions & shortcuts"
---

## How an agent "sees" this repo
1. On start, it loads instruction files: `CLAUDE.md` (Claude Code), `AGENTS.md` (Copilot, Codex, Cursor…), `.github/copilot-instructions.md` (Copilot).
2. It reads files you mention (`@R/01_recode.R`) or that it searches for.
3. It runs commands (R, git) — with your permission.

::: {.note}
[The instruction file is the project brief]{.note-head}
Layout, variable meanings, conventions, guardrails. Here `CLAUDE.md` contains one line —
`@AGENTS.md` — so every tool in the room shares a single source of truth. Change the
brief once and all of them follow it.
:::

## What ours says

```markdown
## Project
Did Latino voters in the Western states shift toward Trump from 2020
to 2024, and does authoritarianism condition that shift?

## Layout
- data/wss_2020_2024.csv  analysis file (read-only; never edit by hand)
- R/01_recode.R           all recoding lives here
- codebooks/              cite these when describing a variable

## Rules
- R + tidyverse, native pipe |>. Minimal comments.
- New recodes go in R/01_recode.R, not in analysis scripts.
- Always report n_obs and n_miss with any model.
- Use survey weights for population estimates; say when you don't.
- Don't push to main without the user's say-so; prefer a branch + PR.
```

## Writing a good AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md
- What the project is (one sentence) and the research question.
- Where things live; which files are read-only.
- Variable definitions and **where to cite them** (codebook).
- Conventions: language, style, where recodes go.
- Guardrails: report N and missingness, use weights, don't push to main.
- Keep it short; agents follow concise rules better than essays.

Personal, all-project preferences go in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.

## Claude Code shortcuts
| Command / key | Does |
|---|---|
| `/init` | Draft a CLAUDE.md from the codebase |
| `/memory` | Edit instruction/memory files |
| `/agents` | Create & manage subagents (e.g., a “codebook checker”) |
| `/clear` | Fresh context (cheap; use between tasks) |
| `/compact` | Summarize long conversation |
| `/model` | Switch model (smaller = cheaper) |
| `/cost`, `/usage` | Track spending |
| `/review` | Review a pull request |
| `/permissions` | What it may run without asking |
| `/resume` | Return to an earlier session |
| `/mcp` | Connect external tools |
| `@file` | Put a file in context |
| `!cmd` | Run a shell command directly |
| `Shift+Tab` | Cycle modes (plan / auto-accept) |
| `Esc` / `Esc Esc` | Interrupt / rewind |

## Copilot shortcuts
| Key / command | Does |
|---|---|
| `Tab` / `Esc` | Accept / dismiss suggestion |
| `Ctrl/Cmd+I` | Inline chat |
| `/explain`, `/fix`, `/tests`, `/doc` | Chat slash commands |
| `@workspace`, `#file` | Add repo or file context |
| Agent mode | Multi-file edits that run commands |

## Division of labor
Copilot is strongest at the **next line** — completions while you type. Claude Code is strongest at the **next task** — *"add income terciles to the recode, rerun it, and show me what changed."* Use both.

## Spending less
- `/clear` between unrelated tasks; long context is re-billed every turn.
- Point at files (`@R/02_analysis.R`) rather than asking it to "look around."
- Plan mode for anything large: approve the plan, then let it execute.
- A smaller model for routine edits and renames.
- One well-specified request beats six vague corrections.

::: {.warn}
[Then verify]{.warn-head}
Agents produce plausible code, and in research code failure is silent. Read the diff,
check the coding against the codebook, report `n_obs` and `n_miss`, and write a test.
That is [Verification](11-verification.qmd).
:::
